みーや小.name: Mīya-gwā
みーや小.desc: A popular local shop recognizable by its roadside sign. You can choose white or green (herbal) noodles, with a bonito-based broth and free fuchiba service. You can enjoy it with a healthy feeling.
t: I ate here in January 2023 😊
Mīya-gwā
This sign is the landmark, lol
I ordered the “sanmai-niku soba (braised pork belly soba).” You can choose white or green noodles, and I chose the herbal noodles.
Braised pork belly soba (sanmai-niku soba)　¥800

The broth is bonito-based and delicious 😋 The noodles are green. I couldn't feel any herbal flavor or taste, but fuchiba (mugwort) came as a free service, so along with it I could eat with a good bitterness and a healthy feeling. Delicious. The braised pork belly was tender too 😋
Rating (9/15): It's just plain tasty 😊 It was bustling with local customers. I thought it's a shop loved by the locals.

むかしむかし.name: Mukashi Mukashi
むかしむかし.desc: A shop run by an owner who is a potter. The tables and tableware are all handmade, and its specialties are the house-made mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) using wood from the hill behind, and hiija (goat) soba with goats raised on that hill. No gamey smell and easy to eat.
t: Relying on the “Nago City Soba Map,” I ate at “Mukashi Mukashi” (October 2020).
“Mukashi Mukashi” along Prefectural Route 84
On the “Nago Soba Map,” “Mukashi Mukashi” was introduced as shop 26 of 41.
The soba map explains “The house-made mokkai soba (made with wood-ash lye) by the potter owner can't be tasted anywhere else!” and has a photo of the “hiija (goat) soba” ^^;

Although I am an Uchinanchu (Okinawan), I have avoided goat since the last time I had hiija soup in junior high school, out of a picky refusal to even try it, but this time I thought it would be a good experience and took on the challenge 💪
Menu (there is no photo, but they say the tables, chairs, and even the tableware inside the shop are all handmade by the owner himself)
Hiija (goat) soba, small　¥1,050

The toppings as they look are indeed beastly, lol But when I ate it, there was absolutely no gamey smell, the meat was tender, and it was just plain tasty ☺ The topping of fuchiba (mugwort) also plays a role in masking odors.

The noodles were mokkai soba made from wood from the hill behind, and the flavor was different from noodles at other shops. The goats are also raised on the hill behind, and you can hear them bleating, which gives a nice peaceful countryside atmosphere.
Rating (9.5/15): Its looks are a shock, lol, but it's just plain tasty ☺ If you're tired of ordinary Okinawa soba, why not give it a try?
PS: While eating I could enjoy it with no gamey smell, but for a while after finishing, my own breath seemed to smell beastly lol Be careful, haha
Also, home-grown shikuwasa and limes were being sold at the counter, so I bought some as souvenirs to put in awamori back home (200 yen total), lol

伊芸サービスエリア（下り）レストラン.name: Igei Service Area (Northbound) Restaurant
伊芸サービスエリア（下り）レストラン.desc: A restaurant in the Igei Service Area (northbound) on the Okinawa Expressway. With its red tile roof and shisa, it has an Okinawan exterior, and serves a classic old-fashioned Okinawa soba topped with green onions, shredded egg, fish cake, and braised pork belly. A reassuring bowl for a break in your travels.
t: I ate here in March 2025 😊
This time, while driving on the Okinawa Expressway, I stopped at the Igei Service Area (northbound) and had “Okinawa soba” 🍜
Igei Service Area (Northbound) Restaurant

When going around eating Okinawa soba, your eyes tend to go to famous shops aimed at tourists or traditional neighborhood diners, but Okinawa soba at service areas like this also catches my interest, since you get to see the “everyday bowl” of Okinawa. The exterior's red tiles catch the eye, giving the feel of “oh, this is Okinawan” at first glance 😆 The shisa on the roof add good flavor too, and it was just the right atmosphere for taking a little break during a trip.
Ticket machine near the entrance

Inside is a spacious area typical of a service area, with a simple diner-like quality, and the lack of pretension was oddly calming. In front of the ticket machine I hesitated a little over what to eat, but this time I chose the basic “Okinawa soba” after all.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
Okinawa soba　¥850

The moment I saw the actual bowl, I thought it was truly a traditional, standard style. In a dark-colored bowl sat green onions, shredded egg, fish cake (kamaboko), and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) — a classic style without gimmicks just by looking at it. With this kind of bowl you can somehow imagine the direction of the flavor before eating, but that “reassurance of it being just as you imagined” is also the good thing about Okinawa soba 😊 First, I took a sip of the broth and it was the type with a pork-bone-based richness. However, rather than being too thick or punchy, my impression was that it was clearly put together as a bowl to eat at a service area. It's not bad, but it didn't make me excited with an “Oh, this is delicious!” — it was a pretty ordinary broth.
Okinawa soba　¥850

The noodles were medium-thick, loose straight noodles with a definite Okinawa soba feel. Lifted up, they also looked just like diner Okinawa soba. But when I ate them they were a bit on the soft side. Personally I would have liked a bit more springiness and bite.

Among the toppings, what left the strongest impression was the braised pork belly, as expected. It was clearly well seasoned just from looking at it. However, there was also a little sinewy texture, and if you expect a softness that gently unravels in your mouth, it's a bit different. It's properly simmered, but not the melt-in-your-mouth type. So for people seeking strong satisfaction from the braised pork belly, it might need one more step. The fish cake, green onions, and shredded egg were the reliable supporting players, tidying up the overall look while properly supporting the old-fashioned Okinawa soba feel.

What I thought while eating this time was that this bowl works as a “reassuring Okinawa soba to eat along the way on a trip,” but if you ask whether I'd stop in just for this, it doesn't quite get there. Comparing within the Okinawa Expressway, I thought the Okinawa soba I ate earlier at “Ajisen Ramen” in the Nakagusuku Service Area was more delicious. The Okinawa soba at this Igei Service Area (northbound) was “ordinary,” in both the good and bad senses. Since I always look for each shop's individuality and a memorable point, in that sense I felt a bit of dissatisfaction.

Still, being able to casually eat this classic-style Okinawa soba at a service area diner is very Okinawan and nice. During sightseeing, between travel legs, when you're a little hungry and don't want to take any adventure but want Okinawa soba, I think it's perfectly fine. It's not flashy, but it felt like they serve a traditional standard Okinawa soba just as it is.
Rating (9/15): My honest take is “ordinary, not exceeding expectations; not so good that I actively want to repeat it” 🙂 But why not try it once when sightseeing in the north? 😆

伊覇そば.name: Iha Soba
伊覇そば.desc: A chicken-broth shop along Route 507. The “Iha Soba,” topped with chicken instead of pig's feet, has a chicken-bone-based flavor not found at other shops. A fresh combination of chicken × Okinawa soba.
t: In January 2023, on the way back from surfing (Itoman City, Suicide Cliff Point), I stopped in since I'd been curious about it for a while ☺
Along Route 507　“Iha Soba”

I went in with no prior information, so for now I ordered the “Iha Soba,” which shares the shop's name. Since the menu said “everything on top,” I thought it would be the usual “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku; the belly part of the pig's torso), pork spare ribs (soki; bone-in pork ribs), and pig's feet (tebichi),” but...
Menu (Iha Soba ¥870)
Iha Soba ¥870　There are soki and braised pork belly, but chicken instead of pig's feet. I hadn't looked at the menu in detail, so I only noticed the difference when it came out ^^;
While thinking “Oh, the toppings are somehow different,” I first took a sip of the broth. “Huh, the broth's taste is different too,” I thought, and took another sip. Yep, different.

Normally, Okinawa soba broth is a blend of pork bone stock, bonito stock, dried small sardines, kelp, and so on, with pork bone emphasized or, for bonito-based ones, bonito emphasized, but this was a taste I'd never experienced at other shops.
So I googled it, and it turns out Iha Soba is “chicken-bone-based.”
I see, so that's why they use chicken in the toppings too ☺
I thought chicken and chicken-stock broth go well with Okinawa soba. It was delicious.
Rating (9.5/15): It's just plain tasty. The chicken and chicken-stock broth are delicious. If you're tired of ordinary soba, why not give it a try? It feels fresh.

伊豆味そば.name: Izumi Soba
伊豆味そば.desc: A queue-guaranteed old-house soba shop standing alone in the mountains of Izumi on the soba road. The No. 1 popular “Izumi Soba” comes with bone-in pork ribs, braised pork belly, and 2 small side dishes. They also have the limited-quantity “Tojin Soba,” a recreation of soba from about 120 years ago.
t: * This article was created by AI (Claude Opus 4.5) with some additions and updates by me 😆
I went to eat here in February 2025 😁😊
For this Okinawa soba outing, I went to “Izumi Soba” in Izumi, Motobu Town 😄
Izumi Soba
Sign-in sheet
Izumi Soba
Signboard along the way to the shop

This shop is near “Mori no Ie,” where I ate the other day, and is also in the mountains 🌿 Following the navigation down a narrow road, an old house suddenly appears alone, surrounded by trees. A big sign with the words “house-made noodles” stands out, greeting you with a red tile roof and a shisa perched on it ✨

When I arrived, there was a “Full” sign at the entrance...! As expected, it's a popular shop. A waiting tent was set up outside, and the system was to wait your turn there. On the sign-in stand were paper and a pen, and you write your name and wait to be called 📝
I waited quite a while that day~ When there's a line, expectations rise too 😆
Menu set up outdoors
Menu set up outdoors
Ticket machine

After waiting a while I finally got inside. There's a ticket machine right at the entrance, so it's a style where you buy a ticket here. You take off your shoes and step up, and the wooden warmth inside is new and clean 🏠 It has the feel of a renovated old house, with exposed ceiling beams giving an open feeling. There was also a sign on the wall reading “Sold out for today,” so it seems it sometimes sells out early.
Inside the shop
Inside the shop
When I sat down, the view out the window was a green landscape with luxuriant hego tree ferns, truly giving the feeling of “eating in the Yanbaru forest” 🌴 The atmosphere is outstanding.
Outside is forest (^0^;)
Menu (again)

Looking at the menu, the “Izumi Soba,” which shares the shop's name, was written as the shop's popular No. 1. It has two kinds of meat, bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki) and braised pork belly (sanmai-niku), plus 2 small side dishes, so it's a good-value menu. They also had “soki soba,” “braised pork belly soba,” and a rare limited-quantity item called “Tojin Soba.” Tojin Soba recreates the origin of Okinawa soba from about 120 years ago, and is apparently a black soy-sauce-based broth 🍜
Naturally this time I decided to order the “Izumi Soba” (¥950), which shares the shop's name.
After waiting a few minutes, the Izumi Soba was brought out on a tray! Beside the soba come pickled bitter melon (goya) and 2 small bowls of tofu. It's full of Okinawan flavor just by looking at it 😊
Izumi soba　¥950
First, as always, I start with the broth. When I took a sip, it was a gentle seasoning with the bonito stock coming through firmly.
Izumi soba　¥950

Next, the noodles. I had been expecting them since they're house-made, and they're medium-thick wavy noodles with a chewy quality 🍜 When you bite, there's a firm springiness, and they cling nicely to the broth. These noodles are quite delicious.

I tried the toppings of bone-in pork ribs and braised pork belly. The seasoning is moderate and not bad, but there's quite a lot of sinewy texture. My impression was that I'd have been happier if they had been simmered a bit more tenderly. The fish cake and green onions were also properly included.
The small side dish of pickled bitter melon has a firm bitterness, and it's surprisingly delicious 😋 It's perfect as a palate cleanser and went well with the soba.

Rating (9.5/15): As an overall impression, because there was a line and I waited quite a while, my expectations had risen, but honestly it felt like it was one step short~ The atmosphere of an old house in the mountains is outstanding. The chewiness of the house-made noodles was good, but the sinewy texture of the toppings bothered me a little. It's a just plain tasty Okinawa soba 😊 Being an old house, the interior is new and clean, the green view from the window is superb, and I'm sure it's a popular shop ✨ I recommend it to those who want to enjoy the atmosphere and savor Okinawa soba slowly.
It might be good to stop by on the way toward Motobu Town, especially to the Churaumi Aquarium or Jungle-ia Okinawa. However, I recommend going at an early time of day, prepared for a line 😄
